↳ Posted by birlibirdie on April 11th, 2012.

Many people must like it, with so many names!

I hate to see a negative comment be the “last word” here. Allow me to note that this tune appears in a classic De Danaan track on the “Selected Jigs, etc.” LP and also in a great medley by Ashley MacIsaac on “Fiddle Music 101”; MacIsaac’s medley starts with a Scottish pipe tune called Christmas Carousing, followed by this tune, then an unknown tune (possibly part of a Ward Allen two-step), and ends with Listen To The Mocking Bird.

Anyhow, I like the tune!

The Maids Of Ardagh, X:9

This is how “Liberton Pipe Band” is played in the Scottish Borders. First part in D then two parts in A. Repeat as necessary and finish on first part.
I’ve also seen this as a four part tune but I’ve never played it that way.

↳ Posted by shanachie on January 3rd, 2022.

Back of the Haggard / Tuar Mór Polka, X:15

This setting is taken from Johnny Leary’s playing in September 1974, recorded and transcribed by Pat Slattery. (The recording is probably available to hear on PJ Teahan’s Handed Down Sliabh Luachra Audio Archive, along with thousands of other recordings of Sliabh Luachra music.).
The second part of the turn is interesting as it is similar to the second part of X:7 , which DonaldK posted six years ago as the Liberton Pipe Band. However Johnny did not appear to play that variation on his commercial recordings.
According to the notes in Terry Moylan’s book, Jack Sweeney (the source) called it Back of the Haggard but Johnny said to name it Tuar Mór because Jack hailed from there.
